Veoh: Open. Personalized. Free. TV. What is Veoh? Veoh is a revolutionary Internet TV service that gives viewers the power to easily discover, watch, and personalize their online viewing experience. With a simple broadband connection Veoh gives you free access to all of the great TV and film studio content, independent productions, and user-generated videos on the Web. ## About Veoh
Veoh Networks positioned itself as an internet television service, founded in 2004 by Dmitry Shapiro and officially launched in February 2007. Shapiro, a Russian immigrant with a background in electrical engineering and web development, previously founded the cybersecurity firm Akonix Systems. The idea for Veoh reportedly came to him during his honeymoon in November 2004, months before YouTube's launch, with the vision of enabling anyone to broadcast video online.
The company's platform was designed to distribute high-quality, long-format videos, aggregating content from major media companies like CBS and ABC alongside independent productions and user-generated material. It distinguished itself from competitors like YouTube by focusing on a downloadable application that organized videos, similar to an iTunes for video, and facilitated a lean-back, television-like viewing experience. This required users to install software, which presented a hurdle to adoption compared to browser-based streaming. Veoh's business model relied on advertising, with plans for behaviorally targeted ads based on users' viewing habits.
Veoh attracted significant attention and approximately $70 million in funding from prominent investors, including Time Warner, Intel Capital, Goldman Sachs, and former Disney CEO Michael Eisner, who also joined the board. At its peak, the service drew over 28 million unique monthly users. However, the company faced substantial challenges. A major lawsuit was filed by Universal Music Group (UMG) in 2007 over copyright infringement. Although Veoh ultimately won the case and subsequent appeals, with courts affirming its protections under the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), the prolonged legal battle drained the company's financial resources. High operational costs, reportedly up to $4 million a month, combined with the economic downturn and the lawsuit's financial strain, proved unsustainable. In February 2010, Veoh filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy. The company was acquired by Qlipso in April 2010 and later by Japanese firm FC2 in 2013, before announcing it would shut down on November 11, 2024, with its content library being moved to FC2 Video.

## About Veoh
Veoh Networks positioned itself as an internet television service, founded in 2004 by Dmitry Shapiro and officially launched in February 2007. Shapiro, a Russian immigrant with a background in electrical engineering and web development, previously founded the cybersecurity firm Akonix Systems. The idea for Veoh reportedly came to him during his honeymoon in November 2004, months before YouTube's launch, with the vision of enabling anyone to broadcast video online.
The company's platform was designed to distribute high-quality, long-format videos, aggregating content from major media companies like CBS and ABC alongside independent productions and user-generated material. It distinguished itself from competitors like YouTube by focusing on a downloadable application that organized videos, similar to an iTunes for video, and facilitated a lean-back, television-like viewing experience. This required users to install software, which presented a hurdle to adoption compared to browser-based streaming. Veoh's business model relied on advertising, with plans for behaviorally targeted ads based on users' viewing habits.
Veoh attracted significant attention and approximately $70 million in funding from prominent investors, including Time Warner, Intel Capital, Goldman Sachs, and former Disney CEO Michael Eisner, who also joined the board. At its peak, the service drew over 28 million unique monthly users. However, the company faced substantial challenges. A major lawsuit was filed by Universal Music Group (UMG) in 2007 over copyright infringement. Although Veoh ultimately won the case and subsequent appeals, with courts affirming its protections under the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), the prolonged legal battle drained the company's financial resources. High operational costs, reportedly up to $4 million a month, combined with the economic downturn and the lawsuit's financial strain, proved unsustainable. In February 2010, Veoh filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy. The company was acquired by Qlipso in April 2010 and later by Japanese firm FC2 in 2013, before announcing it would shut down on November 11, 2024, with its content library being moved to FC2 Video.

# Veoh Networks
## About us
Veoh: Open. Personalized. Free. TV. What is Veoh? Veoh is a revolutionary Internet TV service that gives viewers the power to easily discover, watch, and personalize their online viewing experience. With a simple broadband connection Veoh gives you free access to all of the great TV and film studio content, independent productions, and user-generated videos on the Web. From hit CBS, ABC, WB, ESPN and Comedy Central shows to your favorite YouTube clips, Veoh turns the vast universe of Internet video into an easy-to-use, high-quality, personalized experience that TV fans everywhere can enjoy. Who can publish on Veoh? Veoh is an open platform for content publishers of all sizes and sophistication who want to reach tomorrow’s television audience. Currently more than 100,000 publishers - from forward-thinking, well-known entertainment brands to independent, made-for-the-Web producers - use Veoh to connect with an audience of more than 24 million engaged, influential viewers. In addition, Veoh’s unique publisher optimization program gives publishers powerful tools to help them raise awareness of their content and cultivate loyal viewing audiences.

## About us
Veoh: Open. Personalized. Free. TV. What is Veoh? Veoh is a revolutionary Internet TV service that gives viewers the power to easily discover, watch, and personalize their online viewing experience. With a simple broadband connection Veoh gives you free access to all of the great TV and film studio content, independent productions, and user-generated videos on the Web. From hit CBS, ABC, WB, ESPN and Comedy Central shows to your favorite YouTube clips, Veoh turns the vast universe of Internet video into an easy-to-use, high-quality, personalized experience that TV fans everywhere can enjoy. Who can publish on Veoh? Veoh is an open platform for content publishers of all sizes and sophistication who want to reach tomorrow’s television audience. Currently more than 100,000 publishers - from forward-thinking, well-known entertainment brands to independent, made-for-the-Web producers - use Veoh to connect with an audience of more than 24 million engaged, influential viewers. In addition, Veoh’s unique publisher optimization program gives publishers powerful tools to help them raise awareness of their content and cultivate loyal viewing audiences.

Title: 5 Questions With … Scars On 45
Chunks: 0,1
English indie quintet visits The Recording Academy
English indie quintet Scars On 45 were the recent guest for an installment of The Recording Academy's 5 Questions With … series. Held at The Academy's headquarters in Santa Monica, Calif., Scars On 45 discussed the origin of their name, their songwriting process, the formation of the band, touring the United States, and advice for aspiring musicians, among other topics.
"I can honestly say that we've fallen in love with the place," said vocalist/guitarist Danny Bemrose on touring in the United States. "We can go from playing in New York and Los Angeles [to] San Francisco [and] Whitefish, Montana, and every single person [has] welcomed [us] with open arms."
Formed in Leeds, England, by Bemrose after he suffered a foot injury from playing professional soccer, Scars On 45 features Aimee Driver (vocals), Chris Durling (drums), Stuart Nichols (bass), and David "Nova" Nowakowski (keyboards). The group's sound is described as a combination of the "gentle melodic intensity of Snow Patrol or Keane with the added allure of co-ed vocals." The group derived their name from an interview with Emmylou Harris in which the GRAMMY-winning artist recalled her father advising her not to get any "scars on his 45s" as she played them. After their song "Beauty's Running Wild" was featured on an episode of "CSI: NY," the band was signed to Chop Shop Records and in January released an EP, _Give Me Something_. The band's "**Heart On Fire**" is featured on the soundtrack for the current season of "Grey's Anatomy." Scars On 45 are currently on tour throughout the United States with rock/R&B artist Marc Broussard.
For updates and breaking news, please visit The Recording Academy's social networks on **Facebook**, **Twitter** and **YouTube**.

**Daron Malakian and Scars on Broadway** (previously known as **Scars on Broadway**) is an Armenian-American alternative metal band and solo project of Daron Malakian. The band's self-titled debut album was released in July 2008.

In late 2008, the band entered a hiatus, with Malakian citing a lack of enthusiasm and "his heart not being into touring" as the primary reasons for the band's cessation. Despite reforming with various line-up changes in 2010 and 2012 and announcing a second album, the band ceased any further announcements by 2013. In July 2018, their second album titled _Dictator_ was released, and a third album, _Addicted to the Violence_, was released on July 18th, 2025.
Malakian is also previously known for being the guitarist, composer and second vocalist of the band System of a Down.

### Self-titled debut album (2005–2008)
[edit]
In December 2005, Malakian stated in an interview that he "could release ten solo records tomorrow."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-Solo0-4) He revealed that he has "tons of material laying around", as well as his plans for the future: "After these albums _[Mezmerize_ and _Hypnotize_] I'm gonna go off and do something on my own, just like Serj."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-Solo0-4) Following System of a Down's hiatus in May 2006, Malakian announced his latest project—Scars on Broadway—a band which would include System of a Down drummer John Dolmayan and himself.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-RS-7) Malakian stated "I haven't decided if I'm going to make it a revolving door of musicians or one solid band but it all revolves around my writing."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-8)
Former drummer John Dolmayan
After Malakian and Dolmayan experimented with different musicians, for a period of nine months in 2007 the band took form and forged its sound in intense rehearsals and recording sessions under Malakian's direction at his home studio and Sunset Sound; with musicians Danny Shamoun on keyboards, Dominic Cifarelli on bass, and Franky Perez on guitar and backing vocals. The band begun recording their debut album in September 2007.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-9)

### Self-titled debut album (2005–2008)
The band's website featured a countdown timer, counting down to 15:00 PST on March 28, 2008. Additionally, above the timer, in quotation marks was the phrase "They say it's all about to end." When the countdown ended, the song "They Say" was made available on the site and their Myspace account.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-10)
Scars on Broadway played their first live show April 11, 2008 at the Whisky a Go Go in West Hollywood, California.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-11) They also played with Metallica at KFMA Day 2008 in Tucson, Arizona.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-12) On January 22, 2008, Scars on Broadway were announced to be performing at the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival on April 26, 2008.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-13) They also performed at the sixteenth annual KROQWeenie Roast.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-14)

### Self-titled debut album (2005–2008)
On May 2, 2008, the band announced that their debut album, _Scars on Broadway_, would be released on July 28, 2008.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-16) A week later, the band was signed to Interscope Records.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-17) The first single would be the aforementioned "They Say", which would receive radio airplay, and be made available on _Guitar Hero 5_ and as a downloadable track on _Rock Band_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-20) The music video for the track was released on June 27.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-21)

**Daron Malakian and Scars on Broadway** (previously known as **Scars on Broadway**) is an Armenian-American alternative metal band and solo project of Daron Malakian. The band's self-titled debut album was released in July 2008.
texts.1:
In late 2008, the band entered a hiatus, with Malakian citing a lack of enthusiasm and "his heart not being into touring" as the primary reasons for the band's cessation. Despite reforming with various line-up changes in 2010 and 2012 and announcing a second album, the band ceased any further announcements by 2013. In July 2018, their second album titled _Dictator_ was released, and a third album, _Addicted to the Violence_, was released on July 18th, 2025.
Malakian is also previously known for being the guitarist, composer and second vocalist of the band System of a Down.
texts.2:
### Self-titled debut album (2005–2008)
[edit]
In December 2005, Malakian stated in an interview that he "could release ten solo records tomorrow."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-Solo0-4) He revealed that he has "tons of material laying around", as well as his plans for the future: "After these albums _[Mezmerize_ and _Hypnotize_] I'm gonna go off and do something on my own, just like Serj."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-Solo0-4) Following System of a Down's hiatus in May 2006, Malakian announced his latest project—Scars on Broadway—a band which would include System of a Down drummer John Dolmayan and himself.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-RS-7) Malakian stated "I haven't decided if I'm going to make it a revolving door of musicians or one solid band but it all revolves around my writing."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-8)
Former drummer John Dolmayan
After Malakian and Dolmayan experimented with different musicians, for a period of nine months in 2007 the band took form and forged its sound in intense rehearsals and recording sessions under Malakian's direction at his home studio and Sunset Sound; with musicians Danny Shamoun on keyboards, Dominic Cifarelli on bass, and Franky Perez on guitar and backing vocals. The band begun recording their debut album in September 2007.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-9)
texts.3:
### Self-titled debut album (2005–2008)
The band's website featured a countdown timer, counting down to 15:00 PST on March 28, 2008. Additionally, above the timer, in quotation marks was the phrase "They say it's all about to end." When the countdown ended, the song "They Say" was made available on the site and their Myspace account.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-10)
Scars on Broadway played their first live show April 11, 2008 at the Whisky a Go Go in West Hollywood, California.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-11) They also played with Metallica at KFMA Day 2008 in Tucson, Arizona.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-12) On January 22, 2008, Scars on Broadway were announced to be performing at the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival on April 26, 2008.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-13) They also performed at the sixteenth annual KROQWeenie Roast.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-14)
texts.4:
### Self-titled debut album (2005–2008)
On May 2, 2008, the band announced that their debut album, _Scars on Broadway_, would be released on July 28, 2008.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-16) A week later, the band was signed to Interscope Records.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-17) The first single would be the aforementioned "They Say", which would receive radio airplay, and be made available on _Guitar Hero 5_ and as a downloadable track on _Rock Band_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-20) The music video for the track was released on June 27.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-21)

English indie quintet visits The Recording Academy
English indie quintet Scars On 45 were the recent guest for an installment of The Recording Academy's 5 Questions With … series. Held at The Academy's headquarters in Santa Monica, Calif., Scars On 45 discussed the origin of their name, their songwriting process, the formation of the band, touring the United States, and advice for aspiring musicians, among other topics.
"I can honestly say that we've fallen in love with the place," said vocalist/guitarist Danny Bemrose on touring in the United States. "We can go from playing in New York and Los Angeles [to] San Francisco [and] Whitefish, Montana, and every single person [has] welcomed [us] with open arms."
Formed in Leeds, England, by Bemrose after he suffered a foot injury from playing professional soccer, Scars On 45 features Aimee Driver (vocals), Chris Durling (drums), Stuart Nichols (bass), and David "Nova" Nowakowski (keyboards). The group's sound is described as a combination of the "gentle melodic intensity of Snow Patrol or Keane with the added allure of co-ed vocals." The group derived their name from an interview with Emmylou Harris in which the GRAMMY-winning artist recalled her father advising her not to get any "scars on his 45s" as she played them. After their song "Beauty's Running Wild" was featured on an episode of "CSI: NY," the band was signed to Chop Shop Records and in January released an EP, _Give Me Something_. The band's "**Heart On Fire**" is featured on the soundtrack for the current season of "Grey's Anatomy." Scars On 45 are currently on tour throughout the United States with rock/R&B artist Marc Broussard.
For updates and breaking news, please visit The Recording Academy's social networks on **Facebook**, **Twitter** and **YouTube**.
Click on the "5 Questions With ... interviews" tag below for links to other GRAMMY News stories in this series.

# Scars On Broadway Concert History
84 Concerts
Scars on Broadway is an alternative metal/experimental rock band which formed in 2003 in Los Angeles, California, United States. The band is a side project of Daron Malakian, co-vocalist and guitarist from System of a Down. The band's second album "Dictator", credited to Daron Malakian and Scars on Broadway, was released on July 20, 2018.

**Daron Malakian and Scars on Broadway** (previously known as **Scars on Broadway**) is an Armenian-American alternative metal band and solo project of Daron Malakian. The band's self-titled debut album was released in July 2008.

In late 2008, the band entered a hiatus, with Malakian citing a lack of enthusiasm and "his heart not being into touring" as the primary reasons for the band's cessation. Despite reforming with various line-up changes in 2010 and 2012 and announcing a second album, the band ceased any further announcements by 2013. In July 2018, their second album titled _Dictator_ was released, and a third album, _Addicted to the Violence_, was released on July 18th, 2025.
Malakian is also previously known for being the guitarist, composer and second vocalist of the band System of a Down.

### Self-titled debut album (2005–2008)
[edit]
In December 2005, Malakian stated in an interview that he "could release ten solo records tomorrow."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-Solo0-4) He revealed that he has "tons of material laying around", as well as his plans for the future: "After these albums _[Mezmerize_ and _Hypnotize_] I'm gonna go off and do something on my own, just like Serj."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-Solo0-4) Following System of a Down's hiatus in May 2006, Malakian announced his latest project—Scars on Broadway—a band which would include System of a Down drummer John Dolmayan and himself.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-RS-7) Malakian stated "I haven't decided if I'm going to make it a revolving door of musicians or one solid band but it all revolves around my writing."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-8)
Former drummer John Dolmayan
After Malakian and Dolmayan experimented with different musicians, for a period of nine months in 2007 the band took form and forged its sound in intense rehearsals and recording sessions under Malakian's direction at his home studio and Sunset Sound; with musicians Danny Shamoun on keyboards, Dominic Cifarelli on bass, and Franky Perez on guitar and backing vocals. The band begun recording their debut album in September 2007.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-9)

### Self-titled debut album (2005–2008)
The band's website featured a countdown timer, counting down to 15:00 PST on March 28, 2008. Additionally, above the timer, in quotation marks was the phrase "They say it's all about to end." When the countdown ended, the song "They Say" was made available on the site and their Myspace account.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-10)
Scars on Broadway played their first live show April 11, 2008 at the Whisky a Go Go in West Hollywood, California.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-11) They also played with Metallica at KFMA Day 2008 in Tucson, Arizona.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-12) On January 22, 2008, Scars on Broadway were announced to be performing at the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival on April 26, 2008.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-13) They also performed at the sixteenth annual KROQWeenie Roast.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-14)

### Self-titled debut album (2005–2008)
On May 2, 2008, the band announced that their debut album, _Scars on Broadway_, would be released on July 28, 2008.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-16) A week later, the band was signed to Interscope Records.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-17) The first single would be the aforementioned "They Say", which would receive radio airplay, and be made available on _Guitar Hero 5_ and as a downloadable track on _Rock Band_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-20) The music video for the track was released on June 27.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-21)

Title: 5 Questions With … Scars On 45
Chunks: 0,1
English indie quintet visits The Recording Academy
English indie quintet Scars On 45 were the recent guest for an installment of The Recording Academy's 5 Questions With … series. Held at The Academy's headquarters in Santa Monica, Calif., Scars On 45 discussed the origin of their name, their songwriting process, the formation of the band, touring the United States, and advice for aspiring musicians, among other topics.
"I can honestly say that we've fallen in love with the place," said vocalist/guitarist Danny Bemrose on touring in the United States. "We can go from playing in New York and Los Angeles [to] San Francisco [and] Whitefish, Montana, and every single person [has] welcomed [us] with open arms."
Formed in Leeds, England, by Bemrose after he suffered a foot injury from playing professional soccer, Scars On 45 features Aimee Driver (vocals), Chris Durling (drums), Stuart Nichols (bass), and David "Nova" Nowakowski (keyboards). The group's sound is described as a combination of the "gentle melodic intensity of Snow Patrol or Keane with the added allure of co-ed vocals." The group derived their name from an interview with Emmylou Harris in which the GRAMMY-winning artist recalled her father advising her not to get any "scars on his 45s" as she played them. After their song "Beauty's Running Wild" was featured on an episode of "CSI: NY," the band was signed to Chop Shop Records and in January released an EP, _Give Me Something_. The band's "**Heart On Fire**" is featured on the soundtrack for the current season of "Grey's Anatomy." Scars On 45 are currently on tour throughout the United States with rock/R&B artist Marc Broussard.
For updates and breaking news, please visit The Recording Academy's social networks on **Facebook**, **Twitter** and **YouTube**.

**Daron Malakian and Scars on Broadway** (previously known as **Scars on Broadway**) is an Armenian-American alternative metal band and solo project of Daron Malakian. The band's self-titled debut album was released in July 2008.

In late 2008, the band entered a hiatus, with Malakian citing a lack of enthusiasm and "his heart not being into touring" as the primary reasons for the band's cessation. Despite reforming with various line-up changes in 2010 and 2012 and announcing a second album, the band ceased any further announcements by 2013. In July 2018, their second album titled _Dictator_ was released, and a third album, _Addicted to the Violence_, was released on July 18th, 2025.
Malakian is also previously known for being the guitarist, composer and second vocalist of the band System of a Down.

### Self-titled debut album (2005–2008)
[edit]
In December 2005, Malakian stated in an interview that he "could release ten solo records tomorrow."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-Solo0-4) He revealed that he has "tons of material laying around", as well as his plans for the future: "After these albums _[Mezmerize_ and _Hypnotize_] I'm gonna go off and do something on my own, just like Serj."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-Solo0-4) Following System of a Down's hiatus in May 2006, Malakian announced his latest project—Scars on Broadway—a band which would include System of a Down drummer John Dolmayan and himself.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-RS-7) Malakian stated "I haven't decided if I'm going to make it a revolving door of musicians or one solid band but it all revolves around my writing."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-8)
Former drummer John Dolmayan
After Malakian and Dolmayan experimented with different musicians, for a period of nine months in 2007 the band took form and forged its sound in intense rehearsals and recording sessions under Malakian's direction at his home studio and Sunset Sound; with musicians Danny Shamoun on keyboards, Dominic Cifarelli on bass, and Franky Perez on guitar and backing vocals. The band begun recording their debut album in September 2007.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-9)

### Self-titled debut album (2005–2008)
The band's website featured a countdown timer, counting down to 15:00 PST on March 28, 2008. Additionally, above the timer, in quotation marks was the phrase "They say it's all about to end." When the countdown ended, the song "They Say" was made available on the site and their Myspace account.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-10)
Scars on Broadway played their first live show April 11, 2008 at the Whisky a Go Go in West Hollywood, California.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-11) They also played with Metallica at KFMA Day 2008 in Tucson, Arizona.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-12) On January 22, 2008, Scars on Broadway were announced to be performing at the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival on April 26, 2008.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-13) They also performed at the sixteenth annual KROQWeenie Roast.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-14)

### Self-titled debut album (2005–2008)
On May 2, 2008, the band announced that their debut album, _Scars on Broadway_, would be released on July 28, 2008.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-16) A week later, the band was signed to Interscope Records.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-17) The first single would be the aforementioned "They Say", which would receive radio airplay, and be made available on _Guitar Hero 5_ and as a downloadable track on _Rock Band_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-20) The music video for the track was released on June 27.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-21)

**Daron Malakian and Scars on Broadway** (previously known as **Scars on Broadway**) is an Armenian-American alternative metal band and solo project of Daron Malakian. The band's self-titled debut album was released in July 2008.
texts.1:
In late 2008, the band entered a hiatus, with Malakian citing a lack of enthusiasm and "his heart not being into touring" as the primary reasons for the band's cessation. Despite reforming with various line-up changes in 2010 and 2012 and announcing a second album, the band ceased any further announcements by 2013. In July 2018, their second album titled _Dictator_ was released, and a third album, _Addicted to the Violence_, was released on July 18th, 2025.
Malakian is also previously known for being the guitarist, composer and second vocalist of the band System of a Down.
texts.2:
### Self-titled debut album (2005–2008)
[edit]
In December 2005, Malakian stated in an interview that he "could release ten solo records tomorrow."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-Solo0-4) He revealed that he has "tons of material laying around", as well as his plans for the future: "After these albums _[Mezmerize_ and _Hypnotize_] I'm gonna go off and do something on my own, just like Serj."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-Solo0-4) Following System of a Down's hiatus in May 2006, Malakian announced his latest project—Scars on Broadway—a band which would include System of a Down drummer John Dolmayan and himself.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-RS-7) Malakian stated "I haven't decided if I'm going to make it a revolving door of musicians or one solid band but it all revolves around my writing."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-8)
Former drummer John Dolmayan
After Malakian and Dolmayan experimented with different musicians, for a period of nine months in 2007 the band took form and forged its sound in intense rehearsals and recording sessions under Malakian's direction at his home studio and Sunset Sound; with musicians Danny Shamoun on keyboards, Dominic Cifarelli on bass, and Franky Perez on guitar and backing vocals. The band begun recording their debut album in September 2007.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-9)
texts.3:
### Self-titled debut album (2005–2008)
The band's website featured a countdown timer, counting down to 15:00 PST on March 28, 2008. Additionally, above the timer, in quotation marks was the phrase "They say it's all about to end." When the countdown ended, the song "They Say" was made available on the site and their Myspace account.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-10)
Scars on Broadway played their first live show April 11, 2008 at the Whisky a Go Go in West Hollywood, California.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-11) They also played with Metallica at KFMA Day 2008 in Tucson, Arizona.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-12) On January 22, 2008, Scars on Broadway were announced to be performing at the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival on April 26, 2008.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-13) They also performed at the sixteenth annual KROQWeenie Roast.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-14)
texts.4:
### Self-titled debut album (2005–2008)
On May 2, 2008, the band announced that their debut album, _Scars on Broadway_, would be released on July 28, 2008.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-16) A week later, the band was signed to Interscope Records.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-17) The first single would be the aforementioned "They Say", which would receive radio airplay, and be made available on _Guitar Hero 5_ and as a downloadable track on _Rock Band_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-20) The music video for the track was released on June 27.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-21)

In December 2005, Malakian stated in an interview that he "could release ten solo records tomorrow."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-Solo0-4) He revealed that he has "tons of material laying around", as well as his plans for the future: "After these albums _[Mezmerize_ and _Hypnotize_] I'm gonna go off and do something on my own, just like Serj."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-Solo0-4) Following System of a Down's hiatus in May 2006, Malakian announced his latest project—Scars on Broadway—a band which would include System of a Down drummer John Dolmayan and himself.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-RS-7) Malakian stated "I haven't decided if I'm going to make it a revolving door of musicians or one solid band but it all revolves around my writing."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-8)
Former drummer John Dolmayan
After Malakian and Dolmayan experimented with different musicians, for a period of nine months in 2007 the band took form and forged its sound in intense rehearsals and recording sessions under Malakian's direction at his home studio and Sunset Sound; with musicians Danny Shamoun on keyboards, Dominic Cifarelli on bass, and Franky Perez on guitar and backing vocals. The band begun recording their debut album in September 2007.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-9)

### Self-titled debut album (2005–2008)
The band's website featured a countdown timer, counting down to 15:00 PST on March 28, 2008. Additionally, above the timer, in quotation marks was the phrase "They say it's all about to end." When the countdown ended, the song "They Say" was made available on the site and their Myspace account.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-10)
Scars on Broadway played their first live show April 11, 2008 at the Whisky a Go Go in West Hollywood, California.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-11) They also played with Metallica at KFMA Day 2008 in Tucson, Arizona.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-12) On January 22, 2008, Scars on Broadway were announced to be performing at the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival on April 26, 2008.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-13) They also performed at the sixteenth annual KROQWeenie Roast.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-14)

### Self-titled debut album (2005–2008)
On May 2, 2008, the band announced that their debut album, _Scars on Broadway_, would be released on July 28, 2008.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-16) A week later, the band was signed to Interscope Records.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-17) The first single would be the aforementioned "They Say", which would receive radio airplay, and be made available on _Guitar Hero 5_ and as a downloadable track on _Rock Band_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-20) The music video for the track was released on June 27.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daron_Malakian_and_Scars_on_Broadway#cite_note-21)

# Veoh to target YouTube viewers
By Dawn C. Chmielewski
Feb. 13, 2007 12 AM PT
*
Share via Close extra sharing options   
    *   [Email](mailto:?body=Veoh%20to%20target%20YouTube%20viewers%0A%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.latimes.com%2Farchives%2Fla-xpm-2007-feb-13-fi-veoh13-story.html%0A%0AThe%20online%20site%2C%20which%20launches%20today%2C%20aims%20to%20stand%20out%20with%20longer%20and%20better-quality%20videos.%20Michael%20Eisner%20is%20an%20investor.)  
    *   Facebook  
    *   X

Times Staff Writer
An Internet television service backed by one of Hollywood’s best-known deal makers launches today.
After a year and a half of public testing, Veoh formally opens for business stocked with more than 100,000 videos by amateurs and professionals.
San Diego-based Veoh Networks Inc. is one of an emerging group of video websites seeking to move beyond pratfalls and karaoke. To that end, the company has found an investor with a distinguished Hollywood pedigree: former Walt Disney Co. Chief Executive Michael Eisner, who serves on Veoh’s board of directors.
Advertisement
“You may have cut your teeth on YouTube,” Veoh Chief Executive Dmitry Shapiro said.
“But if you really want to broadcast, if you want to be a producer of video, Veoh is the place you need. It’s for YouTube graduates.”
Veoh is vying for viewers and advertisers in a crowded field, including Google Inc.’s YouTube and Joost, the Internet television venture started by the creators of Kazaa, the file-swapping service that was sued for enabling widespread piracy of songs, movies and TV shows. Veoh seeks to differentiate itself with longer videos, high-quality pictures and sophisticated online publishing tools.

# Veoh to target YouTube viewers
Eisner has been influential in brokering deals between Veoh and content partners. United Talent Agency plans a Veoh channel dedicated to showcasing new talent and content. Celebrity magazine Us Weekly is also creating an entertainment channel.
Advertisement
Like Break.com, Revver Inc. and certain other video sites, Veoh plans to pay publishers based on the audience their videos attract.
“The challenge for Veoh in the short term is more about attracting those talented content creators,” said Jupiter Research senior analyst Joe Laszlo.
Veoh allows producers to automatically distribute videos of any length or picture resolution to multiple sites, including YouTube, Google Video, MySpace and Facebook. The company touts DVD-quality video that can be viewed on a full computer screen, not just in a small window.
Shapiro hopes to make money by collecting transaction fees for videos offered for rental or purchase and by selling ads around free videos.
“There are few advertisers who will want to advertise on short, grainy video clips,” Shapiro said.
YouTube’s short videos still have strong appeal -- 30 million U.S. Web surfers visited the site in January, according to research firm ComScore Media Metrix. Veoh had 657,000 visitors -- a smaller online viewership than Break.com, Metacafe.com or vMix.com.
Advertisement
Although dwarfed by YouTube, Veoh attracted unwanted attention last summer because of its willingness to let its users upload pornographic videos. After facing criticism, the company removed the “adult” category from its site, deleted explicit videos and changed its use terms to prohibit videos containing nudity.
YouTube is engaged in tough negotiations with many television companies over the right to distribute shows.
Digital Music Group Inc. said Monday it had reached a deal with YouTube to make available some television shows to which it controlled the digital rights, including “I Spy” and “My Favorite Martian.”
Veoh is “trying to play a slightly different game than YouTube,” Laszlo said. “I think there’s room for success here. There’s definitely room for failure.”

Times Staff Writer
An Internet television service backed by one of Hollywood’s best-known deal makers launches today.
After a year and a half of public testing, Veoh formally opens for business stocked with more than 100,000 videos by amateurs and professionals.
San Diego-based Veoh Networks Inc. is one of an emerging group of video websites seeking to move beyond pratfalls and karaoke. To that end, the company has found an investor with a distinguished Hollywood pedigree: former Walt Disney Co. Chief Executive Michael Eisner, who serves on Veoh’s board of directors.
Advertisement
“You may have cut your teeth on YouTube,” Veoh Chief Executive Dmitry Shapiro said.
“But if you really want to broadcast, if you want to be a producer of video, Veoh is the place you need. It’s for YouTube graduates.”
Veoh is vying for viewers and advertisers in a crowded field, including Google Inc.’s YouTube and Joost, the Internet television venture started by the creators of Kazaa, the file-swapping service that was sued for enabling widespread piracy of songs, movies and TV shows. Veoh seeks to differentiate itself with longer videos, high-quality pictures and sophisticated online publishing tools.
texts.4:
# Veoh to target YouTube viewers
Eisner has been influential in brokering deals between Veoh and content partners. United Talent Agency plans a Veoh channel dedicated to showcasing new talent and content. Celebrity magazine Us Weekly is also creating an entertainment channel.
Advertisement
Like Break.com, Revver Inc. and certain other video sites, Veoh plans to pay publishers based on the audience their videos attract.
“The challenge for Veoh in the short term is more about attracting those talented content creators,” said Jupiter Research senior analyst Joe Laszlo.
Veoh allows producers to automatically distribute videos of any length or picture resolution to multiple sites, including YouTube, Google Video, MySpace and Facebook. The company touts DVD-quality video that can be viewed on a full computer screen, not just in a small window.
Shapiro hopes to make money by collecting transaction fees for videos offered for rental or purchase and by selling ads around free videos.
“There are few advertisers who will want to advertise on short, grainy video clips,” Shapiro said.
YouTube’s short videos still have strong appeal -- 30 million U.S. Web surfers visited the site in January, according to research firm ComScore Media Metrix. Veoh had 657,000 visitors -- a smaller online viewership than Break.com, Metacafe.com or vMix.com.
Advertisement
Although dwarfed by YouTube, Veoh attracted unwanted attention last summer because of its willingness to let its users upload pornographic videos. After facing criticism, the company removed the “adult” category from its site, deleted explicit videos and changed its use terms to prohibit videos containing nudity.
YouTube is engaged in tough negotiations with many television companies over the right to distribute shows.
Digital Music Group Inc. said Monday it had reached a deal with YouTube to make available some television shows to which it controlled the digital rights, including “I Spy” and “My Favorite Martian.”
Veoh is “trying to play a slightly different game than YouTube,” Laszlo said. “I think there’s room for success here. There’s definitely room for failure.”

Times Staff Writer
An Internet television service backed by one of Hollywood’s best-known deal makers launches today.
After a year and a half of public testing, Veoh formally opens for business stocked with more than 100,000 videos by amateurs and professionals.
San Diego-based Veoh Networks Inc. is one of an emerging group of video websites seeking to move beyond pratfalls and karaoke. To that end, the company has found an investor with a distinguished Hollywood pedigree: former Walt Disney Co. Chief Executive Michael Eisner, who serves on Veoh’s board of directors.
Advertisement
“You may have cut your teeth on YouTube,” Veoh Chief Executive Dmitry Shapiro said.
“But if you really want to broadcast, if you want to be a producer of video, Veoh is the place you need. It’s for YouTube graduates.”
Veoh is vying for viewers and advertisers in a crowded field, including Google Inc.’s YouTube and Joost, the Internet television venture started by the creators of Kazaa, the file-swapping service that was sued for enabling widespread piracy of songs, movies and TV shows. Veoh seeks to differentiate itself with longer videos, high-quality pictures and sophisticated online publishing tools.

# Veoh to target YouTube viewers
Eisner has been influential in brokering deals between Veoh and content partners. United Talent Agency plans a Veoh channel dedicated to showcasing new talent and content. Celebrity magazine Us Weekly is also creating an entertainment channel.
Advertisement
Like Break.com, Revver Inc. and certain other video sites, Veoh plans to pay publishers based on the audience their videos attract.
“The challenge for Veoh in the short term is more about attracting those talented content creators,” said Jupiter Research senior analyst Joe Laszlo.
Veoh allows producers to automatically distribute videos of any length or picture resolution to multiple sites, including YouTube, Google Video, MySpace and Facebook. The company touts DVD-quality video that can be viewed on a full computer screen, not just in a small window.
Shapiro hopes to make money by collecting transaction fees for videos offered for rental or purchase and by selling ads around free videos.
“There are few advertisers who will want to advertise on short, grainy video clips,” Shapiro said.
YouTube’s short videos still have strong appeal -- 30 million U.S. Web surfers visited the site in January, according to research firm ComScore Media Metrix. Veoh had 657,000 visitors -- a smaller online viewership than Break.com, Metacafe.com or vMix.com.
Advertisement
Although dwarfed by YouTube, Veoh attracted unwanted attention last summer because of its willingness to let its users upload pornographic videos. After facing criticism, the company removed the “adult” category from its site, deleted explicit videos and changed its use terms to prohibit videos containing nudity.
YouTube is engaged in tough negotiations with many television companies over the right to distribute shows.
Digital Music Group Inc. said Monday it had reached a deal with YouTube to make available some television shows to which it controlled the digital rights, including “I Spy” and “My Favorite Martian.”
Veoh is “trying to play a slightly different game than YouTube,” Laszlo said. “I think there’s room for success here. There’s definitely room for failure.”
